messages.content: I want the hotel comparison now. Use Penn Quarter, around L'Enfant Plaza, and Capitol Hill. One room for Daniel, Owen, and me, and make sure the room actually sleeps three. Show me what Thursday night really adds before we decide.

I found one strong refundable option in each area. The quoted totals below include the 15.95% D.C. hotel tax and are for one room occupied by two adults and one 12-year-old. I am checking the sleeping setup and cancellation terms separately rather than relying on a generic three-guest search result.
Good. Start with Penn Quarter.

Riggs Washington DC is the strongest Penn Quarter option. The available room is two queen beds, with all three guests listed on the reservation. The refundable rate averages $319 before tax. Friday through Monday is $957 room plus $152.64 tax, or $1,109.64 total. Thursday through Monday is $1,276 room plus $203.52 tax, or $1,479.52 total. There is no mandatory destination fee in this quote. For a Thursday arrival, free cancellation ends at 6:00 p.m. Tuesday, October 8; for Friday arrival, it ends at 6:00 p.m. Wednesday, October 9.
And actual access, not just the neighborhood label.

Riggs is about a 7-minute walk to the National Archives, 12-15 minutes to the National Museum of Natural History and American History, and roughly 18 minutes to the Washington Monument grounds. Gallery Place and Metro Center are both practical. It is the best of the three for restaurants and for returning to the room between museum time and dinner, but it is also the most expensive.
Now L'Enfant. I don't need the Wharf dressed up as if it's next door.

The better fit is Holiday Inn Washington Capitol - National Mall, not a Wharf hotel. A two-queen room is confirmed for three guests. The refundable rate is $259 before tax. Friday through Monday is $777 room plus $123.93 tax, totaling $900.93. Thursday through Monday is $1,036 room plus $165.24 tax, totaling $1,201.24. No mandatory fee appears in the rate. Cancellation is free until 6:00 p.m. Wednesday, October 9 for the Thursday stay, or 6:00 p.m. Thursday, October 10 for the Friday stay.
How does that one work for the museums and monuments?

It is about 5-8 minutes on foot to the Air and Space Museum and the Museum of the Bible, 10-12 minutes to the Hirshhorn, and around 15 minutes to Natural History. L'Enfant Plaza Metro is roughly 6 minutes away. The Lincoln Memorial end of the Mall is still a long walk, about 35-40 minutes, so Metro, Circulator if operating, or a short rideshare makes more sense for that part. The immediate dinner selection is thinner than Penn Quarter.
Capitol Hill next.

Capitol Hill Hotel has a junior suite with one queen bed and a full-size sofa bed; the hotel lists that exact room for three occupants. The refundable rate is $289 before tax. Friday through Monday is $867 room plus $138.29 tax, or $1,005.29 total. Thursday through Monday is $1,156 room plus $184.38 tax, or $1,340.38 total. The displayed quote has no separate mandatory fee. Free cancellation ends at 3:00 p.m. Tuesday, October 8 for Thursday arrival and 3:00 p.m. Wednesday, October 9 for Friday arrival.
I'm less interested in being near the Capitol itself than in whether Owen is going to be sleeping on something marginal for four nights.

Then Capitol Hill Hotel drops behind the other two. The sofa bed is a genuine full-size sleeper, but it is still the weaker setup for a 12-year-old over three or four nights. The hotel is about 8 minutes from the Capitol and Library of Congress, but 20-25 minutes on foot from Air and Space and farther from the central Smithsonian museums. Capitol South Metro helps, though it adds a transfer or extra walking for several stops.
So compare the cost of Thursday itself. Include the airfare difference we already had.

Thursday airfare is $246 more for the family than Friday. Adding the extra hotel night makes the full Thursday-arrival premium $615.88 at Riggs, $546.31 at Holiday Inn Capitol, or $581.09 at Capitol Hill Hotel. Those figures compare the complete four-night trip structure with the corresponding three-night structure, including hotel tax. Parking and breakfast are excluded because neither is needed to make the lodging comparison.
What are we buying for the $546 at the Holiday Inn? Quantify the useful time.

With Thursday arrival, you would likely be in the room around 11:15 p.m. and could start Friday around 9:00 a.m. With the Friday flight, you land at 11:03 a.m.; after reaching the hotel and leaving bags, the realistic start is 12:30-1:00 p.m. Thursday therefore buys about four useful sightseeing hours Friday, possibly five if you want an early timed entry. It does not create another evening, and the late Thursday arrival has little value by itself.
Can the Friday plan still cover the Smithsonian pieces, monuments, and some Capitol time without turning every day into a march?

Yes. Friday afternoon can cover Air and Space plus the Hirshhorn or one nearby museum. Saturday can hold the timed museum that matters most and a second central Smithsonian museum. Sunday can combine the Capitol or Library of Congress with the eastern end of the Mall, then do the monuments around late afternoon and dusk. Monday still leaves roughly 9:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. for one major museum or anything missed. The schedule becomes tight only if two high-priority timed entries are available solely on Friday morning.

Then I don't see Thursday being worth more than five hundred dollars unless ticket availability forces it. Between Riggs and the Holiday Inn, is Riggs giving us $209 more of actual value on the three-night stay?

Not for this itinerary. Riggs costs $208.71 more for Friday through Monday. That buys a better restaurant area, a more polished property, and easier evening access, but it does not improve museum access enough to offset the difference. Holiday Inn is closer to Air and Space, gives you two queen beds, and keeps L'Enfant Plaza available for longer cross-city trips. Riggs is the stronger Penn Quarter hotel; Holiday Inn is the stronger overall value.
All right. Select the Holiday Inn with the Friday arrival, but don't book it yet. Keep Thursday only as the timed-entry fallback. Give me the exact decision and the deadlines I need to watch.

Selected plan, not booked: fly American from O'Hare Friday, October 11 at 8:10 a.m., arrive DCA at 11:03 a.m., and return Monday, October 14 at 6:15 p.m. Airfare for three remains $897. Use Holiday Inn Washington Capitol - National Mall, one two-queen room for all three guests, Friday through Monday. Hotel total is $900.93 including tax, making the current flight-and-hotel total $1,797.93. The refundable hotel rate can be canceled without penalty until 6:00 p.m. Thursday, October 10.

The fallback remains the Thursday, October 10 flight at 7:20 p.m., arriving at 10:13 p.m., with four hotel nights. That structure totals $2,344.24 for airfare and hotel, $546.31 more than Friday. Its hotel cancellation deadline is 6:00 p.m. Wednesday, October 9. Switch only if a high-priority timed entry requires Friday morning; otherwise the extra four to five usable hours do not justify the premium. Nothing has been booked.
